cases.task: Trace the Godot Discord login-session flow into Rails: creation, browser launch, polling/exchange, token persistence, and the Rails validation/issuance boundary.
cases.ownership_boundary: AuthSessionController owns the client operation and persisted credential; DiscordLoginSessionsController owns Rails session validation and access-token issuance.

ownership_evidence.reason: Godot owns the asynchronous login operation and saves the returned token.
Rails creates, validates, consumes, and exchanges OAuth login sessions.

required_evidence.reason: Client API calls define the two Rails requests.
The client owns the exact Rails endpoint construction.
The Rails controller validates polling state and issues an access token transactionally.

forbidden_unsupported_conclusions.pattern: client sends a discord client secret

completion_criteria: Identify both HTTP endpoints and their Rails controller actions.
Distinguish client credential persistence from Rails access-token issuance.

cases.task: Trace a Godot gameplay input packet from its producer through outbound sending, Go websocket/envelope routing, and the authoritative Game handler.
cases.ownership_boundary: Godot produces and sends packet dictionaries; networking admits and routes them; game.Game owns authoritative packet interpretation.

ownership_evidence.reason: Godot owns construction of the gameplay input packet.
Game applies accepted input to authoritative player state.

required_evidence.reason: Outbound client code sends producer output to the network client.
The server websocket reader receives client input.
Envelope decoding establishes packet type and payload.
Gameplay routing calls the room Game with admitted packets.
The authoritative game handler applies input or lifecycle packets.

completion_criteria: Locate the producer, transport handoff, envelope boundary, router, and Game handler.
Do not move authority from Go Game to Godot.

cases.task: Map the respawn lifecycle from Godot request gating through the Go respawn handler and match classification, including the difference between pending respawn and eliminated.
cases.ownership_boundary: GameplayRespawnFlow owns request/UI gating, Game owns respawn mutation, and rules.EvaluateMatch owns active/pending-respawn/eliminated classification.

ownership_evidence.reason: Godot only requests respawn and waits for authoritative confirmation.
Rules owns participation and terminal-match classification.

required_evidence.reason: The client packet producer defines the respawn request.
Client sender dispatches the produced respawn packet.
Inbound routing admits respawn packets and calls Game.
Game selects respawn behavior when packet.Type is PacketTypeRespawn.
The game session mutates respawn state under server authority.
Pending respawn is not elimination while lives remain.

completion_criteria: Show client request gating and server-side mutation.
Explain that a match ends only when rule classification finds every player eliminated.

cases.task: Find every production Godot reader of SPACE_ROCKS_LOCAL_SERVER_PORT and explain which client endpoint each reader controls.
cases.ownership_boundary: ApiConfig owns player-data base URL selection and SessionNetworkTarget owns single-player websocket URL selection; neither reader owns server configuration.

ownership_evidence.reason: ApiConfig reads the key to select the player-data HTTP endpoint.
SessionNetworkTarget reads the same key for the websocket endpoint.

required_evidence.reason: The API configuration validates the port and returns the local HTTP base URL.
The session target validates the port and returns the local websocket URL.

completion_criteria: Name both production readers and their separate endpoint responsibilities.
Do not claim an unverified service-side reader.
